title: MCP Startup Runlayer Accuses Rippling of Allegedly Stealing Its Product Ideas
excerpt: When AI infrastructure meets a "crisis of trust," the competition between big companies and startups is escalating.The startup focusing on the Model Context Pro
content_html:
When AI infrastructure meets a "crisis of trust," the competition between big companies and startups is escalating.

The startup focusing on the Model Context Protocol (MCP) security gateway, Runlayer, has recently filed a lawsuit in court, accusing human resources software company Rippling of stealing its product ideas and trade secrets. This legal dispute reveals the intense competition and potential risks behind enterprise technology procurement in the AI era.

According to the complaint, the two parties had engaged in deep engineering collaboration and product trials for nearly a year. During this time, Runlayer shared its core product roadmap and underlying source code with Rippling, a potential customer. Both parties signed a non-disclosure agreement and a trial agreement containing intellectual property protection clauses. However, the testing was terminated as the two parties failed to reach an agreement on the purchase price.

Not long after, Runlayer's founder and CEO Andrew Berman received information from an internal source that Rippling was secretly developing a clone project almost identical to the startup's product. Based on this, Runlayer believes that the other party is suspected of infringing on trade secrets, breaching the contract, and engaging in unfair competition.

In response to the allegations, Rippling confirmed that it is launching its own MCP gateway but denied the accusation of abusing intellectual property rights, stating that its product is based on its own technological development.

With Anthropic releasing an open-source protocol, the MCP gateway has gradually become a key infrastructure connecting AI models with external data. However, as market competition intensifies, many large companies with strong engineering capabilities often choose to develop in-house, which puts many AI infrastructure startups relying on financing into a difficult dilemma.

content_html_zh:
当人工智能基础设施遇到“信任危机”时，大公司和初创公司之间的竞争正在升级。

专注于模型上下文协议（MCP）安全网关的初创公司Runlayer最近向法院提起诉讼，指控人力资源软件公司Rippling窃取其产品创意和商业机密。 这场法律纠纷揭示了人工智能时代企业技术采购背后的激烈竞争和潜在风险。

诉状称，双方已进行近一年的深度工程合作和产品试验。 在此期间，Runlayer与潜在客户Rippling分享了其核心产品路线图和底层源代码。 双方签署了保密协议和包含知识产权保护条款的试用协议。 但由于双方未能就购买价格达成一致，测试被终止。

不久之后，Runlayer 的创始人兼首席执行官 Andrew Berman 从内部消息来源得知，Rippling 正在秘密开发一个与该初创公司产品几乎相同的克隆项目。 据此，Runlayer认为对方涉嫌侵犯商业秘密、违反合同、从事不正当竞争等行为。

针对这些指控，Rippling 证实正在推出自己的 MCP 网关，但否认了滥用知识产权的指控，并表示其产品是基于自己的技术开发的。

随着Anthropic开源协议的发布，MCP网关逐渐成为连接AI模型与外部数据的关键基础设施。 然而，随着市场竞争的加剧，许多工程能力较强的大公司往往选择内部开发，这让许多依赖融资的AI基础设施初创公司陷入了困境。
